newsitem.title: USA: Centocor sells UK plant to Trinity.
newsitem.headline: Centocor sells UK plant to Trinity.

text.p: Centocor Inc said Wednesday it would take a one-time charge of $4.5 million, or about $0.06 per share, to sell its U.K. diagnostic plant to Trinity Biotech PLC.
Trinity said it is paying $5.5 million in cash and notes for the plant. The company expected to close the transaction iwithin two weeks, depending on the customary consents and approvals.

The 17,000 square feet plant, located in Guildford, U.K., develops and manufactures infectious disease diagnostic tests, including tests for Rubella, Herpes, Syphilis and a new test for Chagas disease, Trinity said, adding Centocor's products line is complementary to its existing diagnostic tests.

Centocor's chief executive David Holveck said in a statement the agreement fitted in Centocor's strategy "to align our diagnostics business to work in synergy with our therapeutic product lines --cardiovascular, autoimmune and cancer." Centocor officials were not immediately asvailable for further comment.

Centocor opened unchanged at 35-1/2 today, while Trinity opened at 2-15/16, up 1/8. A First Call consensus estimate dated June 17 put Centocor's net earnings for the current quarter ending June 30 at $0.07 per share.
